title: GM is betting compute and AI will help it compete with Chinese automakers
slides: It is pouring billions into AI infrastructure
But compute is not the bottleneck Chinese rivals face
Your next GM vehicle may ship with AI features first
Test one AI feature before assuming it works
thread_text:
1. GM's AI bet: can it outcompute China?

General Motors is pouring billions into AI infrastructure, but Chinese carmakers may not be playing the same game. The real bottleneck might be elsewhere.

2. Billions into AI infrastructure

GM's investment is massive, but spending alone doesn't guarantee an edge. Chinese rivals are already deploying AI features at scale, often faster and cheaper.

3. Compute isn't the bottleneck

For Chinese automakers, the challenge isn't raw computing power—it's integrating AI seamlessly into vehicles and user experience. GM's billions might be aimed at the wrong target.

4. Your next GM may ship AI first

GM plans to roll out AI features in upcoming vehicles, possibly ahead of competitors. But shipping early doesn't mean shipping good—especially if the AI isn't tested thoroughly.

5. Test one AI feature yourself

Before assuming GM's AI works, try a demo at a dealership or simulate a use case. Does it actually save you time, or just add complexity? Test it on a real task this week.

General Motors is pouring billions into AI infrastructure to try to outcompute Chinese carmakers.

The bet is that raw computing power will decide who wins the next car market 😳

But compute may not be the real bottleneck for Chinese rivals, who are already shipping AI features at scale.

GM says its next vehicles may ship with AI features first, ahead of competitors.

For anyone who publishes or reviews tech, that means early AI demos will land in showrooms before they're proven 🚗

Don't trust the pitch: test one AI feature on a real task at a dealership this week 💡

Would you buy a car because of its AI, or wait until it's actually useful? 🤔
